PURPOSE OF THIS SMART START INFORMATION PACKET 
 
 
This information packet is intended to promote the safe, correct set-up and integration of the shredding 
system provided by SSI. It will be augmented by the Operation and Service Manual, which will be 
supplied at the time of equipment delivery.
 
  
Appropriate installation and set-up will have a significant impact on the long-term effectiveness and 
reliability of the equipment. Please read this information carefully, and consider how the equipment will be 
installed and used in your facility. This early action on your part will ensure the reduction or elimination of 
avoidable issues that may not otherwise seem important until much later. 
 
 
 
 
WARNING 
 
 
Serious injury or death could result from the improper installation, repair or 
service of this machine. 
 
Repairs and/or service to this machine must only be done by properly trained 
personnel. 
 
 
 
 
 
IMPORTANT 
 
 
It is very important that all personnel operating and maintaining this machine, 
study the sections of this manual that pertain to their particular task before 
beginning or damage to the equipment may occur.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS 
Machine operators and maintenance personnel must alwa ys comply with the safety precautions given in 
this manual and on the stickers and tags attached to the machine. 
 
These safety precautions are given for your safety. Review them carefully before operating the machine 
and before performing general maintenance or repairs. 
 
Supervising personnel should develop additional precaut ions relating to the specific work area and local 
safety regulations.  
 
The PRI-MAX
TM Waste Reducer will provide safe and dependabl e service if operated in accordance with 
the instructions given in this manual. Read and u nderstand this manual and any stickers and tags 
attached to the machine. Failure to do so could result in personal injury or machine damage. 
 
SAFETY SYMBOLS 
Safety symbols and signal words, as shown below ar e used to emphasize all operator, maintenance and 
repair actions which, if not strictly followed, could result in a life-threatening situation, bodily injury or 
damage to the machine. 
 
This is the safety alert symbol. It is used to  alert you to potential personal injury hazards. 
Obey all safety messages that follow this symbol to avoid possible injury or death. 
 
 
 
DANGER 
 
This safety alert and signal word indicat e an imminently hazardous situation, 
which, if not avoided WILL result in DEATH or SERIOUS INJURY. 
 
 
WARNING 
 
This safety alert and signal word indicate a potentially hazardous situation, which, 
if not avoided COULD result in DEATH or SERIOUS INJURY. 
 
 
CA UTION 
This safety alert and signal word indicate a potentially hazardous situation, which, 
if not avoided MAY result in MINOR or MODERATE INJURY.

PROPERTY/EQUIPMENT DAMAGE.

GENERAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS 
 
• Establish a training program for all operators to ensure safe operation. 
• Do not operate the machine unless thoroughly trained or under the supervision of an instructor. 
• Always wear safety equipment such as goggles, ear,  head protection and safety shoes at all times 
when operating the machine. 
• Do not inspect or clean the machine while it is running. Accidental engagement of the machine can 
cause serious injury. 
• Do not operate a damaged or improperly adjusted machine. 
• Never wear loose clothing that can get entangled in the working parts of the machine. 
• Keep all parts of your body away from the working parts of the machine. 
• Always keep critical markings, such as warning stickers legible. 
• To avoid personal injury or machine damage, all maintenance, repair and service must only be 
performed by properly trained personnel. 
• Always stand clear (at least 50ft/15m) away from the waste reducer while in operation. 
• Always stand clear (at least 20ft/6m) when machine is moving. 
• NEVER load any flammable or explosive items into  the waste reducer such as fuel tanks or  
propane bottles. 
• Use appropriate fall protection when working on machine platforms. 
• Be sure the unit is clear of overhead electrical lines prior to folding or unfolding the conveyor. 
• Always have all shields and guards in place before operating machine. 
• Do not process excessively long material that exceeds the top of the feed hopper. 
• Never attempt to process materials in which the waste reducer was not designed. 
• Do not put fingers in bolt holes or between other heavy parts. 
• Always use extreme caution around high-voltage electrical components. 
• Do not stand above hopper/cutting chamber while in operation. 
• Always allow the hydraulic system to cool before performing service work. 
• Always release all pressure in air, fuel, oil and cooling systems before disconnecting lines and fittings. 
• Always replace fasteners with SSI approved parts or equivalent.

MACHINE LOCK-OUT 
 
• Always lock-out the machine when entering the hopper/cutting chamber. 
• Always lock-out and tag-out all power to panels and electric components before servicing. 
 
This is very important!  It is possible to be in the hopper/cutting chamber and out of sight of the control 
panel.  Locking the unit out is the only way to prev ent someone from starting the machine while you are 
inside it! 
 
 
 
 
 
DANGER
Unexpected machine startup can result in death or severe personal injury. 
 
To ensure safety when servicing or inspecting the waste reducer all sources of energy must be switched 
off, locked out and tagged at the source, before work or inspection is started.   
 
On stationary waste reducers, switch off the main br eaker located on the right side of the motor starter 
panel.  (If the unit has more than one breaker, all of them must be switched off, locked out and tagged.) 
On Diesel powered waste reducers isolate the battery using the battery disconnect switch.  
 
Anyone who will be involved in the service or maintenan ce of the waste reducer must place his or her 
own lock on the main breaker or disconnect switch. 
 
Locking out and tagging should be done in accordan ce with plant rules or OSHA approved procedures. 
After the power has been locked out, it is recommended that an attempt be made to start the machine. 
This step confirms that the unit has been correctly locked out. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Motor Starter Panel

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS & WARNINGS 
 
SSI PRI-MAX

The possible sources of energy are: 
 
Electrical energy:  There are several sources of electrical energy to consider. 
 
Control Voltage - The maximum voltage on the control circuit of  the waste reducers is 24 VDC.  Locking 
out the main disconnect switch eliminates this voltage. 
 
Main Power  - The main incoming power will be between 380VAC and 575VAC depending on facility 
requirements.  Locking the main breakers will eliminat e this voltage from all of the circuits except the 
incoming leads on the breakers themselves.  To isol ate this voltage, the breakers feeding the motor 
control panel will have to be turned off and locked out. 
 
Some diesel powered units are equipped with 110VAC he aters on the hydraulic tank and engine block.  
Disconnect (unplug) these to eliminate hazards from this source. 
 
In addition to locking out all energy sources, the following warnings must also be observed. 
 
 
 
 
WARNING 
 
Moving Machinery Hazard. 
 
Un-shredded material falling on an inclined conveyer belt can cause the conveyor 
belt to move unexpectedly even though the power is disconnected.   
 
Remove un-shredded material prior to performing maintenance and/or service. 
 
 
 
WARNING 
 
Moving Machinery Hazard. 
 
Servicing hydraulic cylinder related components with hydraulic pressure present 
in the cylinders after machine shutdown can result in unexpected machine motion. 
 
Manually support loads suspended by cylinders prior to servicing the equipment. 
 
Crack a hose fitting to bleed off any pressure prior to servicing the cylinder 
hydraulics. 
 
 
 
WARNING 
 
Burn Hazard. 
 
Hydraulic fluid and gearbox lubricants can reach high temperatures during 
operation. In addition, mechanical component s that are in contact with hot fluids 
and lubricants will also reach high temperatures. 
 
Allow fluids and lubricants and associated parts to cool before servicing.

DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 
SECTION 
 
1.4 
PAGE 
 
1 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX
TM
 Service Manual – 991274 Rev 0 
ANVIL 
Fixed hardened steel plates, usually welded to the cutting table frame, between which the cutters pass 
and against which the cutters shear, tear or fracture  the waste product. Anvils can be rebuilt to their 
original form. See Cutting Chamber picture below. 
 
AUTOMATIC LUBRICATION (AUTO-LUBE) SYSTEM 
A method of ensuring that selected components are al ways adequately lubricated.  The system consists 
of an electric pump, one or more grease distributi on valves, and several grease distribution lines. Waste 
reducers are equipped with an Auto-Lube System for the cutter shaft bearings. 
 
AUTO REVERSE PROGRAM 
A pre-determined cutter sequence wherein the rotation direction of the cutter shaft is reversed periodically 
to agitate and redistribute the hopper contents. In dual shaft models, shaft reversals are staggered so that 
one shaft continues to operate in the normal direction while the other shaft is reversing. All waste 
reducers are supplied with multiple factory-set Auto Reverse Programs plus one that can be user-
configured.  
 
CHASSIS 
A large assembly, consisting of a fabricated frame wi th several access doors and covers onto which a 
Cutting Table, Discharge Conveyor, HPU, Control Panel and Motor Starter Panel can be mounted or 
installed. A chassis can be converted into a mobile platform (see Semi-Trailer). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CLOSED-LOOP HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT 
A piping arrangement in which pump delivery, afte r passing through other hydraulic components, by-
passes the reservoir and returns directly to pump inlet. Closed-Loop systems require smaller reservoirs, 
are more energy efficient, and are generally more  compact than Open-Loop systems (see Open-Loop 
Hydraulic Circuit). 
 
CONTROL PANEL 
An electrical assembly, consisting of an enclosure that houses the PLC and a variety of other control 
components.

DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 
SECTION 
 
1.4 
PAGE 
 
2 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX
TM
 Service Manual – 991274 Rev 0 
CUTTERS 
Specially shaped hardened steel plates that are an integral part of the cutter shaft.  Cutters have several 
hooks that grab waste material and pull it into and through the anvils, thus shredding, tearing and 
fracturing the material and effecting size reduction. Cutters can be rebuilt to their original form. Cutters 
come in four-hook (High Force) and six-hook (High Volume) styles. See below. 
 
CUTTER SHAFT 
The large rotating part within the cutting chamber that consists of several cutters, cutter spacers, and an 
internal shaft.  Waste reducers are equipped with one or two cutter shafts. See below. 
 
CUTTER STYLE 
There are two styles of cutters available – High Force (HF) and High Volume (HV). HF cutters feature four 
hooks, two for each rotation direction, and are appro priate for processing more resistant waste material. 
HV cutters have six hooks, three for each rotation direction, have a larger sweep diameter, and are 
appropriate for processing less resistant waste material at a higher throughput rate. 
 
 
 
 High Force Cutter    High Volume Cutter

CUTTING CHAMBER 
The zone that is occupied by the rotating cutter shafts and the anvils. 
 
 
 
 
 Cutter Shaft 
 
 
 Cutters 
 
 
 
 
 Anvils 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CUTTING TABLE 
The large mechanical assembly in which waste reducti on actually takes place. It includes a fabricated 
steel frame, one or two cutter shafts, several anvils,  the cutter shaft bearings, and one or more hydraulic 
motors. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 TAIL END HEAD END 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CUTTING TABLE HEAD END 
The end of the cutting table where the hydraulic connections from the HPU are made. See above. 
 
CUTTING TABLE TAIL END 
The end of the cutting table away from where the hy draulic connections from the HPU are made. See 
above.

DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 
SECTION 
 
1.4 
PAGE 
 
4 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX
TM
 Service Manual – 991274 Rev 0 
DISCHARGE CONVEYOR 
A conveyor that carries away the processed waste material. A discharge conveyor may be either 
electrically or hydraulically driven, and may be a straight take-away conveyor, or a bent or folding load-out 
conveyor for elevated discharge. 
 
HOPPER 
The integral part of the cutting table into which waste material is fed or dumped. 
 
HOPPER EXTENSION 
One or more fabricated components that increase the capacity of the hopper. On mobile systems, the 
hopper extension is typically removed during transport. 
 
HYDRAULIC POWER UNIT (HPU) 
An assembly powered by a diesel engine or one or more electric motors and consisting of hydraulic 
pumps, a reservoir, hydraulic valves, a heat exchanger, and various hydraulic control devices.  
 
MOTOR STARTER PANEL 
An electrical assembly for HPUs powered by electric  motors. It consists of an enclosure that houses the 
main breaker, the contactors for supplying power to all electric motors, various circuit protection and 
monitoring devices, and a control voltage power supply. 
 
OPEN-LOOP HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT 
A hydraulic circuit in which the pump inlet is connected to a reservoir and the pump outlet is connected to 
the motor inlet. The motor outlet is connected back to the reservoir. Motor rotation is started, stopped and 
reversed by a directional control valve (see Closed Loop Hydraulic Drive). 
 
PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC) 
A microprocessor-based control devic e that is factory programmed and directs such activities as cutter 
shaft rotation and speed, as well as monitoring numerous remote devices for potential fault conditions.  It 
is housed within the control panel. 
 
SEMI TRAILER 
Mobile waste reducers are mounted on specially designed Semi-Trailers. See below. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
STAND 
A mechanical structure upon which the cutter table is mounted on stationary systems. On systems that 
include a discharge conveyor the stand may include an integral discharge chute and a means of 
supporting the discharge conveyor.

SETUP CONSIDERATIONS/INSTALLATION

2.2 
PAGE 
 
1

OVERVIEW 
The flow of the material to be processed and machine placement are important considerations for safe, 
efficient performance and ease of service.  SSI can provide system des ign assistance to assure optimum 
performance of the total system. The following outlines many important considerations. 
 
Material Feed Method 
• Evaluate type and size of material to be processed prior to specifying components. 
• Determine the feed method: 
 Automatic (rubber belt or steel pan conveyor) 
 Batches (front-end loader, forklift, bucket or grapple) 
• Evaluate “lift over” height when determining type of feeding. 
 
Material Pre-sorting (un-processable materials) 
• Select areas for inspection and sorting prior to feeding. 
• Determine the method for sorting the material to be processed. 
• Determine where un-processable material will be stored. 
 
Hopper Extensions (provides for additional hopper space) 
• Contact SSI to determine if hopper extensions are a practical add-on. 
 
Discharge Chute (directs processed material falling out of the cutting chamber) 
• Chute design must not resist material flow or contribute to bridging or snagging.   
• Generally, the steeper the sides of the discharge chute the better.  
 
Discharge Conveyor (moves material away from the discharge chute) 
• Type of material to be processed determines type of belt material. 
• Belts can be damaged by long items driven from the cutters. 
• Minimum distance between bottom of cutting table and discharge conveyor belt is required as shown 
below for each model.  
 
Clearance is measured at opening where material exits from beneath the cutting table. 
 
Model Minimum Vertical Clearance 
PR770 36 inches 
PR2000 36 inches 
PR4000 43 inches 
PR6000 48 inches 
 
For optimum material flow, the discharge conveyor slope should be about 2 degrees downward until it is 
vertically clear of the cutting table. And should slope no more than 22 degrees upward at any point.

SETUP CONSIDERATIONS/INSTALLATION 
SECTION 
 
2.2 
PAGE 
 
2 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX
TM
 Service Manual - 991214 Rev 0 
 
Cutting Table (the large mechanical assembly consisting of the cutters and anvils, 
shafts, motors and bearings and steel framework enclosure) 
 
Elevation 
• The height at which the cutting table is installed must permit unobstructed feeding and discharge of 
material. Considerations should include: 
• Hopper extensions 
• Material handling equipment 
• Material bale size 
• Facilitating maintenance equipment such as cranes 
• Overhead hazards such as electrical wires 
• Walkways for maintenance or service. 
 
Perimeter Clearance 
• Maintain a perimeter distance of at least 36 inches from machinery for servicing. 
 
Ambient Temperature  
• Drive components are designed to operate at an ambient air temperature of 35°F to 100°F. 
• Operation at higher temperatures may require supplemental cooling. 
• Operation at lower temperatures will require lubricant changes and possibly oil heaters. 
 
Refer to the Lubricant Specifications section in this manual. 
 
Cleanliness 
• Try to keep dust to a minimum.   
• High dust levels will necessitate more frequent cleaning of the fan and cooling fins. 
• The installation should allow for easy removal and replacement of seals and covers. 
 
Foundation Requirements 
• Careless batch loading that result s in frequent “bumping” of the cutting table will result in dynamic 
lateral loads that can compromise the structural inte grity of the foundation.  SSI is not responsible for 
foundation design or ensuring that existing structures are adequate. 
 
Structural Support Requirements 
• If the cutting table is to be mounted on a support structure, consideration must be given to the 
following points: 
 
 Footing requirements for load distribution 
 Load-carrying capacity of the soil 
 Rigidity of the support structure 
 Walkways around cutting table to aid in servicing the unit 
 Static and dynamic design calculations 
 
It is recommended that the support structure be bolted to the foundation.  If SSI is supplying the support 
structure, several mounting holes will be provided in  each pad. Due to fabrication variations, it is 
recommended that mating foundation holes be matched to the stand after it arrives at the installation site.

SETUP CONSIDERATIONS/INSTALLATION 
SECTION 
 
2.2 
PAGE 
 
3 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX
TM
 Service Manual - 991214 Rev 0 
 
Electrical Service 
• No mounting of the electrical panels is provided unless specified on the order. 
• The control panel should be located at either end of  the cutting table, with a clear view of the  
machine's point of operation. 
• The control panel should never be located to the side of the cutting table. 
• Remote emergency stop buttons should be installed in areas near moving machinery. 
• Long wire runs from the electrical panel to the machinery should be avoided. 
• Conduit must be provided for sensing circuits. 
• All wiring must comply with National Electric Code standards. 
• State and local codes may apply. 
 
Refer to the Technical Specifications section of this manual for electrical requirements. A power supply is 
used to produce the necessary control power voltage for the programmable controller (usually 24vdc). 
 
Hydraulic System 
• The hydraulic power unit (HPU) is skid mounted and  is connected to the cutting table with a number 
of fluid lines.  
• The HPU must be located such that none of the large high pressure hoses between the pumps and 
the motors are more than 15 feet long. 
• All hydraulic components and connections must conform to accepted industry standards.  
• Hoses should be used to connect pipe to the HPU and to the machinery to isolate vibration. 
• Rated working pressure of hoses, pipes and fittings  must be equal to or higher than the maximum 
pressure setting on the HPU. 
• Proper sizing of hose and pipes and minimum use of  elbows and fittings help prevent power loss and 
heat buildup. 
• Hoses should be restrained or confined to minimize hazards resulting from sudden pressure changes. 
• Use of hard pipe is required wh enever the connection hoses between the HPU and machinery are 
longer than 15 feet. 
• Pipe should be pickled, oiled and plugged type.  DO NOT USE GALVANIZED OR STANDARD 
BLACK STEEL PIPE!  
• Pipe supports should be used on 7-foot centers or less. 
• Length of the drain line between the motor and HPU should not exceed 20 feet. 
• The case drain line should not rise more than 8 feet above the hydraulic motors at any point. 
 
Important Note:   Hydraulic lines must be thoroughly flushed before connection to the motor. Components to 
assist in flushing hard piping and or hoses are ava ilable from SSI. Contact SSI customer service for 
additional information.

NOTICE
 
 
DANGER
High-Pressure Leaks Hazard. 
 
Hydraulic fluid can penetrate skin resulting in severe personal injury or death. 
 
 
 
 
 
WARNING
Electric Shock Hazard. 
 
External wiring, connections and interlock devices must be installed in accordance 
with the latest national electric codes, local codes, and local electric utility 
requirements.  Improper installation may result in serious injury or death and 
damage to the equipment. 
 
Only competent, authorized  electricians should atte mpt to install, modify, or 
maintain the electrical system. 
 
 
 
 
 
Equipment Damage Hazard. 
 
Failure to follow proper initial start-up or re-start after service procedures may 
result in severe damage to hydraulic components. 
 
Prior to installing and connecting any hydraulic ho ses or sensor cables, carefully read and understand 
Set-Up Considerations in Section 2.  
 
When installing the hydraulic hoses and sensor connections between the HPU and the cutting table, refer 
to the Hydraulic Schematic and Electrical Schematic located in Section 10 in this manual. 
 
Hydraulic Connections 
Ensure that hose sizes and working pressure rati ngs meet the sizes and ratings specified on the 
Hydraulic Schematic. Thoroughly clean the inside of all hoses prior to installation. 
 
1. Connect the large main pressure hoses between  the hydraulic pump and the hydraulic motor.  
 
2. Connect the hydraulic motor case flushing hose s hose between the HPU and the hydraulic motors.  
 
3. Connect the hydraulic motor drain hose between the case motor drain port and the HPU.

HPU TO CUTTING TABLE CONNECTINS 
SECTION 
 
2.5 
PAGE 
 
2

TM
 Service Manual - 991276 Rev 0 
 
Grease Connection 
Connect the push-on grease tube between the Auto-Lube Pump on the HPU and the Auto-Lube Divider 
Valve on the cutting table.  
 
Grease Sensor Connection 
Connect the Auto-Lube Sensor Cable to the sensor switch mounted to the Auto-Lube Divider Valve.  
 
Wire the other end of the sensor cable into  the control panel as indicated on the Electrical Schematic. 
Ensure that the cable in conduit, or is otherwise protected between the cutting table and the HPU. 
 
IMPORTANT NOTE: 
While the smaller motor case flush and drain hoses, as well as the grease tube and sensor cable, may be 
supported by the larger main loop hoses, they should not be tightly tied or strapped to these large hoses. The 
main loop hoses swell and move about when under pressure, and may damage the other hoses, grease tube and 
sensor cable if too tightly secured.
